messages.content:
Policy: Clinical Record Integrity
Definition: AI systems must not generate clinical entries directly into patient records.
Policy Type: C

Candidate risks:
- 1: Unauthorized generation - Health data — Unauthorized generation - Health data is defined as if the model response involves unauthorized generation or disclosure of sensitive health data.
- 2: Unauthorized processing - Health data — Unauthorized processing - Health data is defined as if the model response involves unauthorized processing or misuse of sensitive health data.
- 3: Unauthorized inference/synthesis - Health data — Unauthorized inference/synthesis - Health data is defined as if the model response involves unauthorized inference or synthesis of private health information from public data sources.
- 4: Unauthorized disclosure - Health data — Unauthorized disclosure - Health data is defined as whether the model response facilitates unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health data.
- 5: Data transfer restrictions — Laws and other restrictions can limit or prohibit transferring data. (Concern: Data transfer restrictions can also impact the availability of the data that is required for training an AI model and can lead to ted data.)
  Cross-mappings: nist-value-chain-and-component-integration[broad], mit-ai-causal-risk-entity-human[related], mit-ai-causal-risk-intent-unintentional[related]

matched_risks.justification: Directly addresses the concern of unauthorized AI-generated entries in patient records.
Covers the misuse of health data, which could include unauthorized modifications to patient records.
